items.title: Voyager 1 entering interstellar space
items.claim: Voyager 1 launched in 1977. When did NASA conclude it had crossed into interstellar space?

options.text: Around August 2012, confirmed by NASA in 2013

items.reveal:
Plasma density measurements from the Plasma Wave Subsystem confirmed the crossing.

Voyager 1 still transmits data; its plutonium power source will deplete in the mid-2020s to early 2030s.
items.why: Defining 'interstellar' requires a physical boundary, the heliopause, not a fixed distance.

items.title: The first confirmed exoplanets
items.claim: The first exoplanets confirmed orbited an unusual host. What was it?

options.text: A pulsar (PSR B1257+12), with the discovery announced in 1992

items.reveal_title: Pulsar planets, three years before 51 Pegasi b
items.reveal:
Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail confirmed planets around the millisecond pulsar PSR B1257+12 in 1992.

Mayor and Queloz's 51 Pegasi b (1995) was the first around a sunlike star and won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
items.why: Public memory often centres on the second discovery if the first occurs in an exotic setting.

items.title: What the universe expands into
items.claim: When cosmologists say the universe is expanding, what is the most accurate description of where it expands to?

options.text: The metric of space itself increases distances between unbound objects; there is no external 'outside'

items.reveal_title: Expansion is of the metric, not into a container
items.reveal:
General relativity describes the metric of space evolving with time. The FLRW metric encodes this expansion.

Gravitationally bound systems (galaxies, the Local Group) are not expanding with the cosmic flow.
items.why: Cosmology requires letting go of everyday intuitions about space as a fixed stage.
